newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: RESEARCH ALERT - DBS cuts SIA after results.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - DBS cuts SIA after results.

text.p: DBS Investment Research said on Monday it was cutting its recommendation on Singapore Airlines Ltd to "accumulate" for its local shares and to "reduce" for its foreign shares.

SIA earlier reported a bottom-of-consensus 7.2 percent rise in its net profit to S$560.5 million for the six months to September 30. Its operating profit fell 11.4 percent to S$467.6 million, reflecting a fall in yields.
Shares in the national carrier fell almost six percent on the results. SIA's foreign tranche was down 80 cents at Singapore $13.20 by 0815 GMT.
DBS said in its daily briefing report to clients it expected SIA's full-year operating profit to be affected by lower yields and higher jet fuel costs.
"SIA's FYMar97 interims were disappointing and below market expectations," the report said.
It said it was lowering its recommendation on SIA's local share tranche to accumulate from buy, and its foreign recommendation to reduce from accumulate.
Excluding aircraft sales, SIA's interim company operating profit fell 22.7 percent, DBS noted.
DBS said it expected SIA's full-year results to be adversely affected by the interim performance.
"Due to the uncertainty about SIA's future profitability, we are downgrading our recommendations," it said.

Based on the half-year results, DBS forecast the airline's full-year attributable net profit would total S$1.03 billion, almost unchanged from its 1995/96 result. DBS's previous forecast was for a full-year net profit of S$1.18 billion.
